Upcoming public events from the calendars on Event Calendars, read by Event Index (eventindex.space) from each calendar's iCalendar feed, on Luma, Meetup or elsewhere. Event Index lists each event; it doesn't publish as the organizer, who is named on the item. Events their organizers publish on nostr themselves are read as they are, not copied here. The events belong to their organizers.
The event's title, as its organizer wrote it
When it starts: unix seconds, or YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day event, as in NIP-52
When it ends, in the same form as start; for an all-day event, the day after the last day
When it happens, written out in the event's local time, e.g. Wed 28 Oct 2026, 5:30 PM-8:00 PM EDT
The time zone the event happens in, as an IANA name, e.g. America/New_York
Who hosts it: the name of the calendar it comes from
The calendar it comes from, on Event Calendars
The platform its calendar lives on: luma, meetup, google, mobilizon or gancio; for any other calendar, its feed's host name
Where it happens, as the organizer wrote it: an address, a room or a link
The end's time zone, when it differs from the start's
The start of the event's description, up to 280 characters
cancelled, when the organizer has cancelled it
The organizer's own nostr key (hex), once they've verified it with Event Index
The event's address on Luma, e.g. click-cafe-all-in-2026
The group's name in its Meetup address, e.g. atlantabitdevs
The event's number in its Meetup address
The event's id on Event Index
The event's own page, for sources without a link of their own
The event's image, where its source allows one
A topic or search term, such as the city and the source; repeats

Short looping videos posted on Divine (divine.video), including classic Vines restored from the Vine archive. Each item links to the video file on Divine's media server. The videos belong to their creators.
Title as the creator posted it
Playable MP4 of the video, e.g. https://media.divine.video/<sha256>.mp4
Still image shown before the video plays
Creator's display name. For classic Vines, the name on the original Vine account

Nostr account that posted the video, npub form. Divine creates it behind an email sign-in, so the creator may never have seen it. For classic Vines it is the archive account Divine holds until the original creator claims it
Creator's verified address, e.g. alice@divine.video. Included only when it resolves to creator-npub at the time of listing
The video's id on Divine, the d tag of its kind 34236 event: the file hash for native videos, the original Vine id for classic Vines
SHA-256 hash of the video file, its address on Blossom media servers
Date first posted, YYYY-MM-DD. For classic Vines, the original Vine upload date
Width x height in pixels, e.g. 1080x1920
divine for videos posted on Divine, vine for classic Vines restored from the archive
Original Vine user id, classic Vines only
Loop count on Vine when the archive was taken, classic Vines only
Like count on Vine when the archive was taken, classic Vines only
Spoken or written language, ISO 639-1 code
Divine's capture check result, e.g. verified_mobile or verified_web

Public event calendars from Luma, Meetup and other iCalendar feeds, and organizers who publish their events on nostr, gathered by Event Index (eventindex.space). Their upcoming events are listed on Events. Event Index never publishes as an organizer: an entry's p is the organizer's own key. The directory is in the public domain (CC0); the events belong to their organizers.
The calendar's name, as its organizer gives it
calendar for an organizer's own calendar; aggregator for a feed that only leads to other calendars
The organizer's own nostr key (hex): the publisher of a calendar on nostr, or the key a feed's organizer verified with Event Index
The calendar's name on Event Index: its page is eventindex.space/calendar/<name>
The iCalendar feed the calendar is read from
Where the calendar lives: luma, meetup, google, mobilizon, gancio or nostr; for any other feed, its host name
City or region the calendar is about, e.g. San Diego, US
Geohash of the calendar's usual area
The calendar's id on Luma, e.g. cal-BvuRd9eaZnDGBwy
The group's name in its Meetup address, e.g. sdbitcoiners
A native kind-31924 calendar this entry stands for
A topic or search term, such as the city and the source; repeats
The calendar's own description, from its feed
The calendar's own image, from its feed

Given that the protocol has no way to determine which of these may have been test or spam scenarios, this list will track **real** gigs where a worker was paid by a different person for work the latter earnestly requested.
